newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: U.N. sees no indication of full Iraqi compliance.
newsitem.headline: U.N. sees no indication of full Iraqi compliance.

text.p: A U.N. arms official said on Tuesday that while Iraq had shown readiness to cooperate with United Nations weapons inspectors, there was no indication it would allow U.N. teams full access to all sites.

"They (Iraqis) indicated that they would continue to cooperate with UNSCOM," UNSCOM deputy chairman Charles Duelfer told reporters in Bahrain after a four-day visit to Baghdad. UNSCOM is the U.N. Special Commission in charge of dismantling Iraq's prohibited weapons.
"Iraq did not indicate, however, that it would comply with the requirements...for an immediate, unconditional and unrestricted access to information, locations and documents," Duelfer said.
The U.N. Security Council unanimously warned Iraq on Saturday it would face further sanctions if it did not allow U.N. arms inspectors to search sensitive sites.
The Iraqi leadership rejected the resolution, saying it was unjustified.

Duelfer said the Security Council's warning was a strong message to Iraq that the U.N. "wants us to complete our task in a credible way without seeking to put together a partial monitoring system or an incomplete picture of the Iraqi compliance."
Asked if he saw any possibility for lifting the sanctions imposed on Iraq in 1990 for invading Kuwait, Duelfer said: "I cannot predict how long the embargo will last."

UNSCOM must certify Iraq has no weapons of mass destruction before the United Nations will lift curbs on its oil exports. The U.N. has allowed Baghdad since December to sell $2 billion worth of oil to buy urgently needed goods.
He said Iraq's reaction to future visits by U.N. inspection teams would be crucial before UNSCOM reports to the Security Council in October.
"The Iraqi reaction to the upcoming inspection...site visits is going to be very, very important," he said.

Duelfer had said in Baghdad that the commission was able to account for a large amount of chemical and biological weapons, ballistic missiles and production equipment "but there was a highly important amount which remained unresolved."
